requirements.title: DBLE result value is REAL(A,KIND(0.0D0))
requirements.definition: DBLE(A) has the value REAL(A, KIND(0.0D0)).

pending.dble-integer-real-conversion-value: Use A=-3 and A=5 integers and assert exact double precision values -3.0D0 and 5.0D0; mutating sign or using SNGL must fail.
pending.dble-real-real-conversion-value: Use exactly representable real values such as -2.5 and 0.5 and assert the double precision values equal REAL(A,KIND(0.0D0)), avoiding non-exact decimal conversions.
pending.dble-complex-real-part-conversion-value: Use a complex value such as CMPLX(-4.0,7.0) and assert DBLE equals REAL(A,KIND(0.0D0)), i.e. the real part converted to double precision; mutate by using AIMAG to fail.
pending.dble-boz-real-conversion-delegates-to-re: Use a nonzero actual BOZ literal argument b, for example Z'0000000000000001', in both DBLE(b) and REAL(b,KIND(0.0D0)). Transfer both double precision results to integer storage sequences of the same size using the same integer-array or INT64 mold, and compare the transferred bit patterns elementwise. Do not compare the real values with ==, because the processor-dependent BOZ interpretation may produce a NaN; the absolute numeric value of b remains no portable oracle.
